scope: Proposition 7.1 (Homogeneous tail estimates) of the manuscript “Distortion of countably branching diamonds from midpoint and tree energies” (preprints/Diamond-distortion-from-midpoint-and-tree-energies-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 331 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d71f7eafe03d0d83), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X have a specified coordinate system with dense finite-support vectors. Fix a family P of bounded finite-rank coordinate projections such that every finite support is contained in the range of some P ∈ P. Consider separately the following two hypotheses, each imposed for every P ∈ P, all pure head and tail vectors p = Pp, Py = 0, and every R > 0: ∥y∥2 ≤ C2 R(R − ∥p∥) if ∥p ± y∥ ≤ R, (7.1) ∥p∥2 + a∥y∥2 ≤ R2 if ∥p ± y∥ ≤ R. (7.2) Here C > 0, respectively a > 0, is uniform over P, the vectors, and R. No uniform bound on ∥P∥ or ∥I − P∥ is assumed. For R > 0 and ε > 0, an infinite ε-separated family in the symmetric R-lens at x then satisfies, respectively, ε2 /4 ≤ C2 R(R − ∥x∥), (7.3) ∥x∥2 + aε2 /4 ≤ R2 . (7.4)
